title: add downgrade guard and transactional schema migrations to backup/restore upgrade tooling
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Private deployments require safe, auditable upgrades that can be rolled back only when it is safe. We observed an incident where a failed partial migration left on-prem clusters in an unrecoverable state when operators attempted to rollback. This PR introduces a set of upgrade/rollback safety primitives: version pinning metadata, transactional schema migrations with explicit commit/rollback markers, backup/restore preflight verification, and a downgrade guard that prevents unsafe automatic rollbacks.

What this PR changes (summary):
- Add a transactional migration runner for Postgres migrations used by the private-installer. Migrations are executed inside a DB transaction wrapper that writes a migration state record (migration_id, checksum, status) to a new migrations table; on success the transaction is committed and marker updated.
- Add a downgrade-guard mechanism: installer writes a cluster-level annotation (installer.redwood.com/downgrade-guard) when irreversible migrations have been applied. The uninstall/rollback hooks check this annotation and fail fast with instructions unless the operator explicitly provides a --force-downgrade flag after following restore steps.
- Backup/restore preflight and verification: pre-upgrade hook runs full logical dump + checksum, stores backup metadata in S3 (or provided object store), and verifies restore in a dry-run namespace if requested. A new subcommand installer validate-backup was added to the cli.
- Version pinning: installer now pins schema and migration tooling versions in a cluster-scoped ConfigMap (redwood-installer-versions) and prevents applying a head_branch with mismatched tooling without explicit approval.
- Helm chart changes: added pre-upgrade/post-upgrade hooks for backup verify jobs, lifecycle annotations, and a small templated CronJob for periodic backup verification in long-lived clusters.
- Terraform adjustments: the terraform module used for private deployments now exposes the object-store lifecycle config and adds an optional toggle to enable force-downgrade-exemption for emergency workflows.
- Tests: added unit tests for migration runner, e2e in-kind integration test for upgrade+rollback path, and CI job to run the backup verify flow against a disposable Postgres instance.

Implementation details:
- New DB table: "migrations_state" (migration_id TEXT, checksum TEXT, applied_at TIMESTAMP, status TEXT, operator TEXT). All schema changes go through the migration runner (internal/installer/migrations). Migrations authored with the new runner require an id and checksum header.
- Migration runner supports dry-run and replay modes. Dry-run validates SQL and checksums without applying; replay will re-apply only failed migrations.
- Downgrade guard added to the installer control-plane: when a migration with irreversible=true is applied, the runner flips the cluster annotation and writes a short audit entry into the installer logs and to the audit S3 bucket.
- CLI: installer upgrade --verify-backup will run the preflight backup+verify and refuse to proceed if verification fails. A detailed failure message includes restore instructions and a pointer to the diagnostic bundle.
- Helm: pre-upgrade job template installer-pre-upgrade-backup-verify runs as a Job; on failure the helm upgrade is aborted. The hook is conditional and controlled by values.install.backupVerify.enabled (default true for private installs).
- Terraform: module outputs now include backup_verify_job_name and installer_versions_configmap_id for cross-module wiring.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for migration runner and checksum validation (internal tests pass).
- Integration tests: kind-based upgrade test that goes main->feature changes with irreversible migration, asserts downgrade guard prevents rollback, then performs a tested restore and validates resume.
- Staging run on an internal on-prem cluster (redwood-sim-02) ran this upgrade path with a seeded dataset. Observability dashboards added for migration duration and preflight backup size.

Rollout notes / operator guidance:
1) Run `installer validate-backup --bucket <backup-bucket>` and ensure success.
2) `installer upgrade --verify-backup` will perform preflight checks; inspect logs if it fails.
3) If a downgrade is required after irreversible migrations, follow documented restore steps in docs/operators/private-upgrade-rollback.md and use --force-downgrade only after restoration is confirmed.

Related: linear keys ENG-3421 ENG-3488; Jira SUP-901 for a customer incident that motivated this change.

Checklist:
- [x] migration runner implementation
- [x] helm hooks and templates
- [x] terraform outputs and toggles
- [x] backup preflight CLI and job
- [x] unit and integration tests
- [x] docs and operator guidance

review_comments: Carlos Ramirez: Can we make the downgrade guard opt-in for clusters that have an operator-managed backup process? Suggest adding a values flag and document the operational flow.
Asha Patel: Added values.install.downgradeGuard.enabled and documented the opt-in behavior. By default it's enabled for safety in private installs.
Mei Lin: Migration runner looks good; please add a metric for migration_attempts_total and migration_failures_total so SRE can alert.
Asha Patel: Added Prometheus metrics and a small dashboard tile. Updated tests to assert metrics are emitted on failure.
Jordan Blake: Terraform output change looks fine but ensure backward compatibility for users pinning outputs by name.
Asha Patel: Kept the old outputs and added the new ones (backwards-compatible).
release_notes: Adds transactional schema migrations, backup preflight verification, and a downgrade guard for private-installer upgrades. Includes new CLI validation subcommands, helm hooks, and terraform outputs. Operators should run backup verification before performing upgrades; irreversible migrations will set a guard that prevents accidental rollbacks.
